caption_hook: Nebraska has been a coal swamp, a chalk seafloor and a grassland full of rhinos.

layers.name: SAND HILLS DUNES
layers.what: Wind piled up sand into dunes across the middle of the state, covering about a quarter of Nebraska. Grass now holds them in place, but they can wake up in a drought.
layers.bonus: It is the largest dune field in the Western Hemisphere, and it sits on top of the Ogallala Aquifer.

layers.name: OGALLALA GROUP
layers.hook: Rivers of sand and a rhino pit
layers.what: Rivers off the Rockies spread gravel and sand over the High Plains. It now holds the Ogallala Aquifer, which waters farms from South Dakota to Texas. Some of that water fell as rain long ago.
layers.bonus: At Ashfall, rhinos and camels were buried alive by ash from a volcano in Idaho.

layers.name: BRULE FORMATION
layers.what: Soft clay and ash mudstone that forms the base of Chimney Rock and Scotts Bluff. Oregon Trail pioneers used both towers as signposts on the long road west.
layers.bonus: Chimney Rock appears on Nebraska's state quarter, minted in 2006.

layers.name: NIOBRARA CHALK
layers.what: The Western Interior Seaway left this pale chalk, built from the tiny shells of plankton. It holds fossils of mosasaurs and huge predatory fish. Tiny plankton shells make up most of the rock.
layers.bonus: The formation is named for the Niobrara River, where it was first described.

layers.name: INDIAN CAVE SANDSTONE
layers.what: Rivers and deltas built this soft sandstone when Nebraska sat near a tropical coast. Weather later carved a shallow cave into its cliffs above the Missouri River.
layers.bonus: The cave walls are marked with old petroglyphs, now protected in Indian Cave State Park.
